hints: Look closely at the chemistry in the diagram. Region X has charged O atoms and a phosphate group, while Y and Z are long chains of CH2 groups. Which end looks polar and which looks non-polar?

Compare the two tails carefully. Y is all single bonds and straight, but Z has a C=C double bond that makes a kink. Remember how a kinked unsaturated tail affects packing and movement in the hydrophobic core.
walkthrough:
**Identify regions X, Y and Z**

Region X at the top contains glycerol plus phosphate and R group with O- charges. That is the hydrophilic head.

Regions Y and Z below are long hydrocarbon fatty acid tails made of CH2 and CH3 groups. They are non-polar.

**Match hydrophilic and hydrophobic behaviour**

Hydrophilic means water-loving, so region X attracts water molecules by forming hydrogen bonds and polar interactions.

Hydrophobic means water-fearing, so regions Y and Z repel polar molecules and water. They form the water-free interior of the bilayer.

**Spot saturated versus unsaturated**

Region Y is straight with only C-C single bonds, so it is saturated and packs tightly.

Region Z has a CH=CH double bond that creates a bend or kink. This kink pushes neighbouring tails apart, increases fluidity and increases permeability of the hydrophobic region. So only Z does this job.

options.A: Incorrect. X is the hydrophilic head, so it attracts water, not repels polar molecules, and Y and Z are hydrophobic, not water-attracting.
options.B: Close but not quite. Y and Z do repel polar molecules and X does attract water, but Y alone does not increase permeability. Only the kinked unsaturated tail Z does that.
options.C: Incorrect. Both Y and Z repel polar molecules, not just X, and only Z with its double bond kink increases permeability, not both tails.
options.D: Correct. Z (unsaturated kinked tail) increases permeability, Y and Z (both hydrophobic tails) repel polar molecules, and X (charged hydrophilic head) attracts water.
